Root cause

* pthread_mutex_init() in cpukit/posix/src/mutexinit.c wrote flags into the mutex object before completing attribute validation. With protocol PTHREAD_PRIO_PROTECT and an out-of-range prio ceiling, init returned EINVAL but left a partially-initialized object. Subsequent pthread_mutex_trylock()/destroy() validated the object via magic/flags and proceeded, returning EBUSY or crashing instead of EINVAL.

Fix

* Compute flags locally and defer writing any state to the mutex until after validation (including prio ceiling translation) succeeds. Then write flags and initialize the thread queue, nest level, priority ceiling node and scheduler. This ensures a failed init leaves the caller’s object unmodified per POSIX.

Tests (reproduction and regression)

* Extended testsuites/psxtests/psx05/init.c with test_mutex_failed_init_invalid_ceiling():
* memset a pthread_mutex_t to 0xa5
* set attr protocol to PTHREAD_PRIO_PROTECT
* set ceiling to sched_get_priority_max(SCHED_FIFO) + 1 (out of range)
* verify pthread_mutex_init() returns EINVAL
* verify subsequent pthread_mutex_trylock() and pthread_mutex_destroy() on the same object return EINVAL
